title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Pluto
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Pluto, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his buried endings. Pluto is unknown to Picatrix, found in 1930 and outside the world the book describes at every point. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of Picatrix's doctrine, never the source's own words. Named for the Roman lord of the underworld, it is read as the far, dark hinge of the set: a course that closes on it ends in the buried kind of ending, the small death of a matter before the next sign begins.
